parsed.attack: The invite goes to a sibling who is already standing in the family group chat that currently serves as the audit trail - a channel that costs nothing, contains everyone, and already puts a name on every message. They are being asked to install a narrower thing to replace a thing that mostly works, in exchange for logging discipline, and they can get the answer they need by typing 'did anyone give the 8pm one' where they already are. Even at full conversion the loop saturates at the two to four siblings caring for one parent, and there is no mechanism whatever by which one household reaches the next, so every subsequent household is hand-recruited from caregiver forums whose posting cadence is weekly, not the three-day cycle a compounding loop needs.
parsed.strongest_defence: Attribution is precisely what the chat fails at - it is unsearchable at 3am and nobody can reconstruct who gave what - so the sibling who nearly double-dosed their mother installs the same day they are asked, and r/AgingParents and AgingCare carry thousands of exactly that post.
parsed.verdict_reason: The in-family invite is real and fast but closes at three or four people, and there is no household-to-household mechanism at all.
